2607.19235.title: MeetingToM: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs on Theory-of-Mind Reasoning in Multi-Party Meetings
2607.19235.paper_summary: Theory of Mind (ToM), the ability to infer other's beliefs, intentions, and states of knowledge, is central to social interaction, yet remains challenging for current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), especially in multi-party meetings where cues are distributed across speech and behavior. Existing multimodal ToM benchmarks mainly focus on video-grounded question answering over overt, externally verifiable signals, and provide limited coverage of latent social states and group dynamics. We introduce MeetingToM, a benchmark for complex social behavior reasoning in naturalistic multi-party meetings. MeetingToM targets meeting-specific phenomena such as \textbf{pseudo-consensus}, where apparent agreement masks private dissent under social pressure. The benchmark is hierarchically organized to evaluate ToM at increasing levels of social granularity, including (i) subject-level mental state prediction, (ii) dyadic-level addressee understanding, and (iii) group-level consensus reasoning. We provide a unified evaluation protocol and conduct systematic analyses of representative MLLMs, revealing persistent limitations in integrating non-verbal cues, inferring hidden attitudes, and distinguishing genuine consensus from pseudo-consensus. Our results highlight key challenges and establish MeetingToM as a testbed for advancing meeting-grounded ToM in multimodal models.
2607.19235.paper_summary_zh: 心智理論（ToM），即推測他人信念、意圖和知識狀態的能力，對社交互動至關重要，但對於當前的多模態大型語言模型（MLLMs）來說，仍然是一個挑戰，特別是在多方會議中，線索分布在語言和行為之間。現有的多模態ToM基準主要集中在基於視頻的問題回答上，針對明顯的、可外部驗證的信號，對潛在社會狀態和群體動態的覆蓋有限。我們引入了MeetingToM，這是一個針對自然多方會議中複雜社交行為推理的基準。MeetingToM針對會議特定現象，例如\textbf{偽共識}，即表面上的一致掩蓋了在社會壓力下的私人異議。該基準以層級方式組織，以評估在不同社會細粒度層次上的ToM，包括（i）主體層級的心理狀態預測，（ii）雙人層級的受話者理解，以及（iii）群體層級的共識推理。我們提供了一個統一的評估協議，並對代表性的MLLMs進行系統分析，揭示在整合非語言線索、推斷隱藏態度以及區分真實共識與偽共識方面的持續限制。我們的結果突顯了關鍵挑戰，並確立MeetingToM作為推進多模態模型中會議基礎ToM的測試平台。
